claims.evidence: This is stated with a clarifying explanation in the introduction.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers do not contain myosin II.
claims.source: These actin filament bundles do not contain myosin II, and dorsal stress fibers are thus unable to contract (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Cramer et al., 1997; Tojkander et al., 2011; Oakes et al., 2012; Tee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers are unable to contract.
claims.source: These actin filament bundles do not contain myosin II, and dorsal stress fibers are thus unable to contract (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Cramer et al., 1997; Tojkander et al., 2011; Oakes et al., 2012; Tee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers interact with contractile transverse arcs and link them to focal adhesions.
claims.source: However, dorsal stress fibers interact with contractile transverse arcs and link them to focal adhesions.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claims.claim: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern.
claims.source: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles, which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern and undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claims.claim: Transverse arcs undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
claims.source: Transverse arcs are curved actin bundles, which display periodic α-actinin – myosin II pattern and undergo retrograde flow towards the cell center in migrating cells.
claims.evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claims.claim: Transverse arcs are derived from α-actinin- and tropomyosin/myosin II- decorated actin filament populations nucleated at the lamellipodium of motile cells.
claims.source: They are derived from α-actinin- and tropomyosin/myosin II- decorated actin filament populations nucleated at the lamellipodium of motile cells (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tojkander et al., 2011; Burnette et al., 2011; 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: In fibroblasts and melanoma cells, filopodial actin bundles can be recycled for formation of transverse arc-like contractile actomyosin bundles.
claims.source: In fibroblasts and melanoma cells, filopodial actin bundles can be recycled for formation of transverse arc –like contractile actomyosin bundles (Nemethova et al., 2008; Anderson et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Ventral stress fibers are contractile actomyosin bundles anchored to focal adhesions at both ends.
claims.source: Ventral stress fibers are defined as contractile actomyosin bundles, which are anchored to focal adhesions at their both ends.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a definition in the introduction.

claims.claim: The central regions of ventral stress fibers can bend towards the dorsal surface of the lamellum.
claims.source: Despite their nomenclature, the central regions of ventral stress fibers can bend towards the dorsal surface of the lamellum (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Schulze et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Migrating cells display thick ventral stress fibers that are typically oriented perpendicularly to the direction of migration.
claims.source: Migrating cells display thick ventral stress fibers that are typically oriented perpendicularly to the direction of migration, and thinner ventral stress fibers that are often located at the cell rear or below the nucleus.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation in the introduction.

claims.claim: Thick ventral stress fibers constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells.
claims.source: At least the thick ventral stress fibers, which constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells, are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claims.claim: Thick ventral stress fibers are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs.
claims.source: At least the thick ventral stress fibers, which constitute the major force-generating actomyosin bundles in migrating cells, are derived from the pre-existing network of dorsal stress fibers and transverse arcs. However, the underlying mechanism has remained poorly understood (Burridge et al., 2013; Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge, though the mechanism was not understood.

claims.claim: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata.
claims.source: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata and they disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix (Mochitate et al., 1991; Discher et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Stress fibers disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix.
claims.source: Stress fibers are typically present only in cells grown on rigid substrata and they disassemble upon cell detachment from the matrix (Mochitate et al., 1991; Discher et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: After applying fluid shear stress, stress fibers align along the orientation of flow direction in endothelial cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, after applying fluid shear stress, stress fibers align along the orientation of flow direction in endothelial cells (Sato and Ohashi, 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces.
claims.source: Also focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces, and applying external tensile force promotes their enlargement (Chrzanowska-Wodnicka and Burridge, 1996; Pelham et al., 1999; Riveline et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Applying external tensile force promotes enlargement of focal adhesions.
claims.source: Also focal adhesions develop only on rigid surfaces, and applying external tensile force promotes their enlargement (Chrzanowska-Wodnicka and Burridge, 1996; Pelham et al., 1999; Riveline et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas.
claims.source: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas, whose activities and interactions with other focal adhesion components can be modulated by forces of ~∼10–50 pN range (Sawada et al., 2006; del Rio et al., 2009; Ehrlicher et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Activities and interactions of mechano-sensitive focal adhesion proteins can be modulated by forces of ~10–50 pN range.
claims.source: Focal adhesions contain several mechano-sensitive proteins, including talin, filamin and p130Cas, whose activities and interactions with other focal adhesion components can be modulated by forces of ~∼10–50 pN range (Sawada et al., 2006; del Rio et al., 2009; Ehrlicher et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Protein compositions of focal adhesions are regulated by tension supplied by myosin II activity and external forces applied to the cell.
claims.source: Furthermore, the protein compositions of focal adhesions are regulated by tension supplied by myosin II activity and external forces applied to the cell (Zaidel-Bar et al., 2007; Kuo et al., 2011; Schiller et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Possible effects of tensile forces on actin filament assembly at focal adhesions have remained elusive.
claims.source: Importantly, despite wealth of information concerning mechanosensitive focal adhesion proteins, possible effects of tensile forces on actin filament assembly at focal adhesions have remained elusive.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claims.claim: Mechanisms by which tension contributes to the alignment of stress fibers have not been reported.
claims.source: Furthermore, the mechanisms by which tension contributes to the alignment of stress fibers and actin dynamics within these actomyosin bundles have not been reported.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claims.claim: Formation of mature contractile actin bundles from their precursors is a mechanosensitive process.
claims.source: Here we reveal that formation of mature contractile actin bundles from their precursors is a mechanosensitive process.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction.

claims.claim: Arc fusion during centripetal flow is accompanied by increased contractility.
claims.source: We show that arc fusion during centripetal flow is accompanied by increased contractility that inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP, thus insuring formation of ventral stress fibers.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by traction force microscopy data.

claims.claim: Activation of AMPK allows generation of contractile ventral stress fibers in cells growing on compliant matrix.
claims.source: Conversely, activation of AMPK allows generation of contractile ventral stress fibers in cells growing on compliant matrix, where their formation is normally prevented.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and supported by AICAR treatment experiments.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers and arcs are present in U2OS cells grown on compliant matrix.
claims.source: By plating U2OS cells on soft (0.5 kPa) and stiff (64 kPa) substrata, we revealed that dorsal stress fibers and arcs are also present in cells grown on compliant matrix.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from experiments comparing cells on different substrate stiffnesses.

claims.claim: Ventral stress fiber assembly is compromised in U2OS cells grown on compliant matrix.
claims.source: In contrast, ventral stress fiber assembly is compromised under these conditions (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from experiments comparing cells on different substrate stiffnesses, with supporting figure.

claims.claim: 89% of U2OS cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: While 89% of cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers, only 10% of cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers as defined by presence of straight, contractile actin bundles connected to focal adhesions at each end.
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments on different substrate stiffnesses.

claims.claim: Only 10% of U2OS cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: While 89% of cells plated on 64 kPa matrix contained ventral stress fibers, only 10% of cells plated on 0.5 kPa matrix exhibited ventral stress fibers as defined by presence of straight, contractile actin bundles connected to focal adhesions at each end.
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from experiments on different substrate stiffnesses.

claims.claim: Generation of ventral stress fibers is the mechanosensitive phase in the formation of the stress fiber network.
claims.source: Thus, generation of ventral stress fibers appears to be the mechanosensitive phase in the formation of the stress fiber network.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the substrate stiffness experiments.

claims.claim: Thin arc precursors fuse with each other during centripetal flow.
claims.source: Interestingly, live-imaging of GFP-CaP3 -transfected cells revealed that the thin arc precursors fused with each other to form thicker actomyosin bundles during their flow towards the cell center (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Arc fusion often initiates at the sites where arcs are connected to elongating dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: Fusion appeared to often initiate at the sites where arcs were connected to elongating dorsal stress fibers (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Homotypic coalescence of tropomyosin-4/myosin II foci and α-actinin foci of adjacent arcs occurs during the fusion process.
claims.source: Live-imaging of cells expressing CFP-α-actinin and YFP-tropomyosin-4 demonstrated that homotypic coalescence of tropomyosin-4/myosin II foci and α-actinin foci of adjacent arcs occurred during the fusion process in all observed cases (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments with dual-labeled cells.

claims.claim: The periodic α-actinin — myosin II pattern is retained during arc fusion.
claims.source: Thus, thin arc precursors fuse with each other during centripetal flow to generate thicker actomyosin bundles, where the periodic α-actinin — myosin II pattern is retained.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the live-cell imaging experiments showing homotypic coalescence.

claims.claim: Thick ventral stress fibers exhibit stronger traction forces to focal adhesions compared to forces applied by dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: These experiments revealed that thick ventral stress fibers exhibit stronger traction forces to focal adhesions as compared to forces applied by dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2A and B), similarly to what was recently demonstrated with model-based traction force microscopy by Soine et al. (2015).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from traction force microscopy experiments.

claims.claim: Spacing between individual CaP-3 foci decreases as arcs flow towards the cell center and become thicker.
claims.source: Furthermore, spacing between individual CaP-3 foci, which co-localize with α-actinin in stress fibers (Small and Gimona, 1998), decreased as the arcs flowed towards the cell center and become thicker as detected both from several fixed samples and live-cell imaging experiments (representative examples are shown Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from both fixed and live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Decreased spacing between CaP-3 foci correlates with increased contractility of arcs.
claims.source: This correlates well with the increased contractility of the structures (Aratyn-Schaus et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Distal focal adhesions linked via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of arcs turn and align along the direction of the arc during maturation.
claims.source: These experiments revealed that the 'distal' focal adhesions, linked via dorsal stress fibers to the ends of the arc, turned and aligned along the direction of arc.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments tracking focal adhesion alignment.

claims.claim: Focal adhesions linked to the central region of arcs do not display alignment during arc maturation.
claims.source: In contrast, focal adhesions linked to the central region of the arc did not display similar alignment during the process.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments tracking focal adhesion alignment.

claims.claim: Alignment of distal focal adhesions correlates with arc fusion.
claims.source: Alignment of 'distal' focal adhesions correlated with arc fusion, and was accompanied by enlargement of adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Alignment of distal focal adhesions is accompanied by enlargement of adhesions.
claims.source: Alignment of 'distal' focal adhesions correlated with arc fusion, and was accompanied by enlargement of adhesions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Arc fusion during centripetal flow correlates with increased contractility, consequent enlargement of distal focal adhesions and their alignment along the direction of the actomyosin bundle.
claims.source: Thus, arc fusion during centripetal flow correlates with their increased contractility, consequent enlargement of distal focal adhesions and their alignment along the direction of the actomyosin bundle.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the traction force and focal adhesion alignment experiments.

claims.claim: Arc fusion leads to formation of a directed ventral stress fiber containing one properly aligned large focal adhesion at both ends.
claims.source: Eventually, this leads to formation of a directed ventral stress fiber, containing one properly aligned large focal adhesion at its both ends.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the live-cell imaging experiments tracking the maturation process.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers in U2OS cells elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions with a rate of ∼0.25 μm/min.
claims.source: In U2OS cells, this 'vectorial' actin polymerization promotes elongation of the actin filament bundle with a rate of ∼0.25 μm/min (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006).
claims.evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge from previous work.

claims.claim: Focal adhesions may contain actin filament populations not directly associated with vectorial actin polymerization and elongation of dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: In addition, focal adhesions may contain other actin filament populations that are not directly associated with vectorial actin polymerization and consequent elongation of dorsal stress fibers.
claims.evidence: This is stated as a consideration based on the presence of multiple tropomyosin isoforms and actin-regulating proteins in focal adhesions.

claims.claim: Several tropomyosin isoforms localize to focal adhesions.
claims.source: This is because several tropomyosin isoforms, which are likely to decorate distinct actin filament populations, localize to focal adhesions (Tojkander et al., 2011) and because several proteins involved in actin polymerization regulate actin dynamics at focal adhesions (e.g. Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Skau et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence.
claims.source: Furthermore, FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence (Videos 1 and 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), whereas FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery that is indicative of vectorial actin polymerization (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from FRAP experiments.

claims.claim: FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery indicative of vectorial actin polymerization.
claims.source: Furthermore, FRAP experiments performed at focal adhesions show rapid, uniform recovery of GFP-actin fluorescence (Videos 1 and 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 2), whereas FRAP experiments performed at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions exhibit treadmilling-like recovery that is indicative of vectorial actin polymerization (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Tee et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from FRAP experiments with supporting citations.

claims.claim: Ventral stress fibers do not elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
claims.source: Therefore, in contrast to dorsal stress fibers, ventral stress fibers do not elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from FRAP and photoactivation experiments comparing dorsal and ventral stress fibers.

claims.claim: MLCK inhibitor ML-7 induces rapid disassembly of most contractile ventral stress fibers and transverse arcs without affecting integrity of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: This compound induced rapid disassembly of most contractile ventral stress fibers and transverse arcs, without affecting integrity of non-contractile dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers in cells treated for 2 h with ML-7 are ∼1.5 times longer compared to control cells.
claims.source: Importantly, dorsal stress fibers in cells treated for 2 h with ML-7 were ∼1.5 times longer compared to the ones in control cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claims.claim: Disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor Y27632 leads to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from inhibitor treatment experiments.

claims.claim: Over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN) prevents assembly of contractile arcs.
claims.source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN) leads to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: Similarly, disruption of contractile stress fibers by ROCK inhibitor, Y27632, or by over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN), which prevents assembly of contractile arcs (Tojkander et al., 2011), led to formation of abnormally long dorsal stress fibers (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments.

claims.claim: Abnormally long dorsal stress fibers in Rif-TN expressing cells continue to elongate throughout the entire observation period.
claims.source: Importantly, live-imaging of GFP-actin expressing cells revealed that the abnormally long dorsal stress in Rif-TN transfected cells continued to elongate throughout the entire observation period.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Dorsal stress fibers in Rif-TN expressing cells occasionally bend or fuse with another elongating dorsal stress fiber during their uncontrolled elongation.
claims.source: During their uncontrolled elongation, the dorsal stress fibers of Rif-TN expressing cells occasionally bent or fused with another elongating dorsal stress fiber initiated from the opposite side of the cell (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A; Videos 3 and 4).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live-cell imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Ablated ventral stress fibers display approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization compared to intact contractile fibers.
claims.source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from laser ablation and FRAP experiments.

claims.claim: Vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile ventral stress fibers is very slow (∼0.02 μm/min).
claims.source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from FRAP experiments.

claims.claim: Ablated ventral stress fibers display vectorial actin polymerization at a rate of ∼0.23 μm/min.
claims.source: Whereas vectorial actin polymerization in intact contractile fibers was very slow (∼0,02 μm/min), ablated ventral stress fibers displayed approximately 10-fold higher rate of vectorial actin polymerization (∼0,23 μm/min), which is comparable to the one of dorsal stress fibers (Figure 3A and B, and data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from laser ablation and FRAP experiments.

claims.claim: Photoactivation experiments demonstrate specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: Importantly, also photoactivation experiments on PA-GFP-actin expressing cells demonstrated specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers and lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the focal adhesions located at the ends of non-ablated ventral stress fibers within the same cell (Figure 3C and D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from photoactivation experiments.

claims.claim: Non-ablated ventral stress fibers lack vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions.
claims.source: Importantly, also photoactivation experiments on PA-GFP-actin expressing cells demonstrated specific elongation of laser ablated ventral stress fibers and lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the focal adhesions located at the ends of non-ablated ventral stress fibers within the same cell (Figure 3C and D).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from photoactivation experiments.

claims.claim: Vectorial actin filament assembly that promotes elongation of dorsal stress fibers is inhibited in focal adhesions located at the tips of contractile ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: These data demonstrate that vectorial actin filament assembly, which promotes elongation of dorsal stress fibers, is inhibited in focal adhesions located at the tips of contractile ventral stress fibers.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the FRAP and photoactivation experiments.

claims.claim: Tension applied by myosin II–mediated contractility is important for inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions located at the ends of ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: Furthermore, laser ablation experiments as well as assays with MLCK and ROCK inhibitors, and dominant inactive Rif provide evidence that tension applied by myosin II–mediated contractility is important for inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions located at the ends of ventral stress fibers.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from multiple experimental approaches.

claims.claim: Dia1 formin has been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions.
claims.source: Two proteins promoting actin filament elongation, Dia1 formin and vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP), have been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Oakes et al., 2012; Watanabe et al., 1999; Gateva et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: VASP has been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions.
claims.source: Two proteins promoting actin filament elongation, Dia1 formin and vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP), have been linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions (Hotulainen and Lappalainen, 2006; Oakes et al., 2012; Watanabe et al., 1999; Gateva et al., 2014; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: VASP and its family members Mena and Evl accumulate to focal adhesions.
claims.source: Because from these proteins only VASP, and its family members Mena and Evl, accumulate to focal adhesions (Reinhard et al., 1992; Gertler et al., 1996; Lambrechts et al., 2000; Hoffman et al., 2006), we focused on examining the possible role of VASP in tension-controlled actin filament assembly in focal adhesions.
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Zyxin mediates recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling.
claims.source: Previous studies demonstrated zyxin-mediated recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling (Smith et al., 2010; Hoffman et al., 2012) and mechanosensitive recruitment of VASP to epithelial zonula adherens (Leerberg et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: VASP is recruited to epithelial zonula adherens in a mechanosensitive manner.
claims.source: Previous studies demonstrated zyxin-mediated recruitment of VASP to the sites of stress fiber repair and remodelling (Smith et al., 2010; Hoffman et al., 2012) and mechanosensitive recruitment of VASP to epithelial zonula adherens (Leerberg et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated with a supporting citation indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: VASP localizes to focal adhesions located at the tips of both dorsal and ventral stress fibers.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claims.claim: Regulation of VASP localization does not explain the lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: Therefore, regulation of VASP localization does not offer an explanation for the lack of vectorial actin polymerization at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion from the VASP localization experiments.

claims.claim: Phosphorylation of VASP at Ser239 and Thr278 inhibits its actin filament binding and polymerization activities.

claims.evidence: This is stated with supporting citations indicating established knowledge.

claims.claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP is enriched in focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers.
claims.source: Although the signal with this antibody was weak, it specifically stained focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers, whereas enrichment of phospho-Ser239 VASP to adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers was not detected (Figure 4D, E and F).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claims.claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP is not enriched in focal adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers.
claims.source: Although the signal with this antibody was weak, it specifically stained focal adhesions located at the tips of ventral stress fibers, whereas enrichment of phospho-Ser239 VASP to adhesions at the tips of dorsal stress fibers was not detected (Figure 4D, E and F).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence experiments.

claims.claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP levels are >2-fold elevated in cells transfected with dominant active RhoA.
claims.source: In line with the data presented above, both phospo-Ser239 (Figure 4G and H) and phospho-Thr278 (data not shown) levels were >2-fold elevated in the cell population transfected with a construct expressing dominant active RhoA, whereas phospo-Ser239 levels were ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix and unable to form contractile ventral stress fibers (Figure 4I and J).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from Western blotting experiments.

claims.claim: Phospho-Ser239 VASP levels are ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix.
claims.source: In line with the data presented above, both phospo-Ser239 (Figure 4G and H) and phospho-Thr278 (data not shown) levels were >2-fold elevated in the cell population transfected with a construct expressing dominant active RhoA, whereas phospo-Ser239 levels were ∼5-fold diminished in cells plated on soft matrix and unable to form contractile ventral stress fibers (Figure 4I and J).
claims.evidence: This is quantitative data from Western blotting experiments.

claims.claim: VASP phosphorylation in focal adhesions correlates with increased contractility of stress fibers.
claims.source: Thus, VASP phosphorylation in focal adhesions correlates with increased contractility of stress fibers.

results.result: Ventral stress fiber formation is mechanosensitive and requires rigid substrata. U2OS cells on soft (0.5 kPa) matrix retain dorsal stress fibers and arcs but show compromised ventral stress fiber assembly (10% vs 89% on 64 kPa matrix), identifying ventral stress fiber generation as the mechanosensitive phase.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C52 provide converging evidence from substrate stiffness experiments with clear quantitative data (C50, C51) and appropriate controls. The experimental design directly tests mechanosensitivity by comparing different substrate stiffnesses, and the conclusion (C52) logically follows from the observations.

results.result: Transverse arcs fuse laterally during centripetal flow to form thicker actomyosin bundles. Live-cell imaging reveals that thin arc precursors fuse with each other, often initiating at dorsal stress fiber connection sites, with homotypic coalescence of tropomyosin-4/myosin II and α-actinin foci while retaining the periodic pattern.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C4 and C53-C56 are well-supported by live-cell imaging data (Figure 1B-D). The observations of arc fusion, initiation sites, and homotypic coalescence provide direct visual evidence. The retention of periodic patterns (C56) is a logical inference from the homotypic coalescence data (C55).

results.result: Arc fusion correlates with increased contractility and focal adhesion maturation. Traction force microscopy shows ventral stress fibers exert stronger forces than dorsal stress fibers. During maturation, spacing between CaP-3 foci decreases, distal focal adhesions align and enlarge along the arc direction, ultimately forming directed ventral stress fibers.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C46, C57-C65 are supported by traction force microscopy (Figure 2A-B), live-cell imaging of focal adhesion dynamics (Figure 2—supplement 1), and measurements of CaP-3 spacing (Figure 1—supplement 1C-D). The correlation between decreased spacing and increased contractility (C59) is supported by citation to prior work. The overall conclusion (C64-C65) logically integrates the observations.

results.result: Tension from myosin II-mediated contractility inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions of ventral stress fibers. FRAP and photoactivation experiments show ventral stress fibers lack vectorial actin polymerization (~0.02 μm/min) compared to dorsal stress fibers (~0.25 μm/min). Laser ablation or myosin II inhibition restores vectorial polymerization (~0.23 μm/min).
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C85 are supported by multiple complementary approaches: FRAP (Figure 2C-E), photoactivation (Figure 2F), laser ablation (Figure 3A-D), and pharmacological inhibition (Figure 2—supplement 3). The quantitative data are consistent across methods, and appropriate controls (non-ablated fibers within same cells) strengthen the conclusions. The ~10-fold difference in polymerization rates provides strong evidence for tension-dependent inhibition.

results.result: AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of VASP at Ser239/Thr278 inhibits vectorial actin polymerization at focal adhesions. Phospho-VASP is enriched at ventral but not dorsal stress fiber focal adhesions. AMPK inhibitors (compound C, KT5823) prevent VASP phosphorylation, eliminate ventral stress fibers, and cause abnormally long dorsal stress fibers, phenocopying the constitutively active VASP mutant.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C91-C98, C100-C104, C106-C107 are supported by immunofluorescence (Figure 4D-F), Western blotting (Figure 4G-J, 5C), and phenotypic analysis (Figure 5A-E). The differential localization of phospho-VASP (C94-C95) is demonstrated, though the antibody signal is noted as weak. The correlation between VASP phosphorylation and contractility (C96-C98) is shown across multiple conditions. The phenotypic similarity between AMPK inhibition and constitutively active VASP mutant (C104, C106) provides strong support for the proposed mechanism.

results.result: AMPK activation by AICAR is sufficient to induce ventral stress fiber formation on compliant matrix. AICAR treatment increases VASP Ser239 phosphorylation, causes early ventral stress fiber maturation with shorter dorsal stress fibers, and rescues ventral stress fiber formation on soft (0.5 kPa) matrix where it is normally prevented.
results.evaluation: Claims C47, C108-C114, C117-C118 are supported by Western blotting (Figure 6B), immunofluorescence (Figure 6A), and quantification on different substrates (Figure 6C-D). The rescue of ventral stress fiber formation on soft matrix (C114) is particularly compelling evidence that AMPK-mediated VASP phosphorylation is sufficient to bypass the normal mechanosensitive requirement. The similarity to VASP depletion phenotype (C112) supports specificity.

results.result: VASP is important for mechanosensitive actin filament assembly in focal adhesions. VASP knockdown cells show ~3-fold decrease in ablation-induced vectorial actin polymerization at ventral stress fiber tips compared to controls.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C116 are supported by photoablation experiments in VASP knockdown cells (Figure 7). The ~3-fold reduction is quantified and statistically significant. However, the incomplete inhibition (C150) indicates other proteins also contribute, which is appropriately acknowledged.

results.result: ADF/cofilin-mediated disassembly of non-contractile stress fibers is required for stress fiber maturation. Cofilin-1 localizes specifically to dorsal stress fibers but not contractile ventral stress fibers or arcs. Cofilin-1 depletion causes abnormally long dorsal stress fibers and impaired arc fusion, leading to defective ventral stress fiber formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C132-C143 are supported by immunofluorescence showing differential cofilin localization (Figure 9A-B, Figure 9—supplement 1A-C) and cofilin-1 knockdown experiments (Figure 9C-D, Figure 9—supplement 1E-F). The selective localization to non-contractile structures (C132-C133) is clearly demonstrated. The knockdown phenotype (C138-C140) provides functional evidence for cofilin's role in dorsal stress fiber turnover and arc fusion.

results.result: During arc maturation, only focal adhesions at arc ends are retained while central focal adhesions and associated dorsal stress fibers disassemble. Terminal focal adhesions elongate during maturation, while central adhesions diminish and disappear. Dorsal stress fibers oriented perpendicularly to arcs or extending beyond arcs disassemble.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C124 are supported by live-cell imaging experiments (Figure 8, Figure 8—supplement 1). The differential fate of terminal vs. central focal adhesions (C121-C122) and selective disassembly of specific dorsal stress fiber populations (C123-C124) are directly observed. This provides important mechanistic detail about the maturation process.

results.result: Myosin-derived tension controls both actin filament assembly and disassembly to ensure proper stress fiber generation and alignment. Tension-mediated maturation of focal adhesions inhibits vectorial actin polymerization (at least partially via VASP phosphorylation), which is essential for proper alignment and contractility. Mechanosensitive cofilin binding leads to disassembly of non-contractile regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C45, C149, C153-C155, C160-C163 represent the integrated model synthesizing the major findings. These conclusions are well-supported by the collective evidence from substrate stiffness, arc fusion, traction force, VASP phosphorylation, and cofilin localization experiments. The model logically connects the observations into a coherent mechanistic framework.

results.result: Background knowledge establishing the context for stress fiber research. This includes the roles of cell migration, actin structures, stress fiber categories (dorsal, transverse arcs, ventral), their known properties, mechanosensitivity of stress fibers and focal adhesions, and identification of knowledge gaps regarding assembly mechanisms and tension effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C44 represent established knowledge from the literature, appropriately cited throughout. These provide necessary context and identify the gaps (C17, C43, C44) that the study addresses. The claims are well-supported by citations to prior work.

results.result: Dorsal stress fibers elongate through vectorial actin polymerization at ~0.25 μm/min. Focal adhesions contain multiple actin filament populations with different dynamics. FRAP at focal adhesions shows rapid uniform recovery, while FRAP at dorsal stress fiber regions below focal adhesions shows treadmilling-like recovery indicative of vectorial polymerization.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are supported by FRAP experiments (Videos 1-2, Figure 2—supplement 2) and prior work (C66). The distinction between focal adhesion actin dynamics and stress fiber elongation (C69-C70) is important for interpreting the results. The presence of multiple actin populations (C67-C68) is a reasonable inference supported by citations.

results.result: Background on VASP and its regulation. VASP and Dia1 formin are linked to actin polymerization in focal adhesions. VASP and family members (Mena, Evl) accumulate at focal adhesions. VASP phosphorylation at Ser239/Thr278 is regulated by PKA, PKG, and AMPK. Prior work showed zyxin-mediated VASP recruitment and mechanosensitive VASP recruitment to adherens junctions.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C90, C99 represent established knowledge appropriately cited from the literature. These provide necessary background for understanding the VASP experiments and their significance.

results.result: Background on ADF/cofilin proteins. ADF/cofilins are essential regulators of F-actin disassembly in eukaryotes. They preferentially bind flexible actin filaments in vitro, do not localize to contractile stress fibers in intact cells but translocate upon substrate relaxation, and affect actin filament bending mechanics. Cofilin-1 is the major isoform in non-muscle cells. Cofilin-1 depletion causes defects in multiple actin structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C131, C137 represent established knowledge appropriately cited from the literature. These provide necessary background for understanding the cofilin experiments and their significance.

results.result: Discussion and model elaboration. This includes details of the working model, discussion of VASP's multiple roles, consideration of other proteins (formins, palladin, tropomyosins), discussion of focal adhesion mechanosensitivity and force regimes, speculation about regulation mechanisms, and consideration of alternative explanations for mechanosensitivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C144-C175 represent discussion points, model elaboration, and speculation appropriately qualified in the text. The working model (C144-C155) synthesizes the findings. Additional observations (C167-C168) provide supporting evidence. Speculation (C151, C166, C172) is appropriately identified. Discussion of prior work (C156-C165, C169-C175) provides context.

results.result: Inhibition of vectorial actin polymerization halts stress fiber elongation and ensures proper contractility. Contractile stress fibers are protected from ADF/cofilin-mediated severing.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C8, C10 are logical inferences from the experimental data. C7-C8 follow from the VASP phosphorylation and vectorial polymerization inhibition data. C10 follows from the cofilin localization data. These are reasonable conclusions though somewhat inferential.

results.result: Over-expression of dominant inactive Rif GTPase (Rif-TN) prevents assembly of contractile arcs.
results.evaluation: Claim C75 is stated with a supporting citation to prior work (Tojkander et al., 2011) and is used as a tool to disrupt contractile structures in the current study. This is established knowledge appropriately applied.

results.result: Over-expression of constitutively active VASP mutant occasionally produces curly actin filament bundles containing myosin II but with defective contractile properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C105 and C135 describe an interesting observation, but the characterization is limited. The curly bundles are noted as 'occasional' (C105), and the defective contractility (C135) is stated as 'data not shown.' While cofilin-1 localization to these structures (C134) is shown, the incomplete characterization limits confidence in the interpretation.
